text: HR meeting transcript Everyone and everything here is fictional. Anna is the HR manager at Muster AG. Leo works in product at Lonio.
Can you hear me okay? You're a bit quiet.
Is this better? I'm in the small meeting room, the big one is taken. Sorry, let me just close the door.

Much better. So, thanks for making the time. The idea today is simple. We want your new employees to give us everything once, so that you stop chasing them for the same information three times. I just want to understand what you need from them.
Yes, please. Right now it's a mess. I have a Word document, then an Excel file, and then I type everything into the portals by hand. Last month I spent a full afternoon on two new hires.
Okay. And how many people do you hire in a year?
Around twenty. More in summer. We're about a hundred and fifty people now, mostly here in Zurich.
Good. Let's start with the biggest pain. What takes you the most time?
Source tax, without any doubt. Because I never know up front who has to answer those questions. So I send the whole questionnaire to everybody, and the Swiss people get annoyed, and they call me.
So who actually needs to answer them?
All the non-Swiss employees. Simple as that. If you don't have a Swiss passport, you do source tax.
Okay, that's clear. And the questionnaire itself is what?

I use the Zurich calculator on the canton's website. The one that gives you the tariff code. I sit with the answers and click through it. For everybody I use Zurich, by the way. I know it's not exactly how it works, but that's what we do for now.
Understood. We'll keep that for now. Let's leave source tax for a moment, I want to come back to it. What about the basics? Name, address, that kind of thing?
Yes, I need the address, obviously. The full address. Street, number, postcode, town, country. We post a lot of documents to people, so it has to be complete.
Anything else on the address?
No, no. Just a normal address, the way you would write it on an envelope.
Great. Do you also want a photo? Some customers ask for one.
Oh, that would be so nice, actually. For the badges. Right now people come to reception and they take a picture with a phone, and it's always terrible. Could the form ask for a photo?
It could. Do you want that from day one?
Hmm. Let me think. No, you know what, security is changing the badge system next year anyway. Let's not do that now. Forget the photo for the moment, we'll talk about it next year.
Okay, no photo. Now, the pension fund. How does that work today?
We're with Pensionskasse Muster. They have a portal, it's quite old. I'll send you some screenshots of it after this call, that's easier than me explaining it.
Perfect. What do you need for the fund that you don't have?
Well, I always need to know when the person starts. I need their first working day. That's the number one thing, and I ask them to confirm it, because it moves more often than you'd think.
It moves?

Oh yes. People negotiate with their old employer, they get out a week earlier. We had a problem with exactly that, with Julia. She moved her first working day to the 15th of March, and I didn't update it. And of course the fund then has the wrong date, because insurance starts on the first of the following month. So for her that was the first of April, and I had entered something else. I got a very unfriendly letter.
Ouch.
Yes. Unless somebody starts exactly on the first, of course, then it's just that day. Anyway. It took weeks to fix.
Sorry, one second, someone's at my door. [pause] Okay, I'm back, sorry. Where were we?
The Julia story. It doesn't matter.
Right. What else about the employee affects the fund? Are they married, things like that?
Yes, the civil status. They ask for that. And if someone is married, they want the date of birth of the husband or wife.
And what are the options in that list?
I'd have to look. You'll see it in the screenshots. Single, married, divorced, I think widowed. But now that you ask, we do have one colleague in a registered partnership. Daniel, in finance.
How did you enter him?
That was before my time. I've never had to enter one myself. I honestly don't know what the fund's screen does in that case, or if they want the partner's details too.
Okay. Noted. Can I go back to source tax? You said all non-Swiss employees.

Yes. Well, wait. No, that's actually not right. I'm thinking of Maria in sales, she's Portuguese, and she doesn't do source tax at all. She has a C permit. So, not the people with a C permit. They're treated like Swiss people for this. I forget that because I do it so automatically.
Okay, so non-Swiss, but not with a C permit. Is that everything?
I think so. Do you want some numbers on how long this takes? I could get that for you from our payroll person.
Sure, send it if it's easy. Do people need anything from you on the first day? Laptops, things like that? I just want to see if that belongs in the same form.

IT does laptops, they have their own process, keep them out of this, please. They'd never agree anyway. What I would love is if the form could remind people to bring their permit. Half of them forget.
We can look at the wording later. Let's see. What happens when someone's married, on the source tax side? Does that change anything?

It changes the questions in the calculator, yes. Whether the husband or wife works. Oh, and that reminds me, it also changes who has to do it at all. If you're married to someone Swiss, or to someone with a C permit, and that person lives here, then you don't do source tax either. Tomás in logistics, for example. Brazilian, B permit, but his wife is Swiss, and they live in Winterthur. So no source tax for him. I always have to check that one by hand.
So you need to know about the spouse as well.
Yes. Their nationality, their permit if they have one, and that they live here. I ask them by email, and it takes forever.
Okay. Anything else on who needs to do it? I'd rather hear all of it now.

I think that's it. Let me look at my list. Hold on. [pause] Oh, the people living abroad. Sorry. We have a few who live across the border. Stefan lives in Konstanz, and there's a woman in the warehouse who lives in Liechtenstein. Those people do source tax because they work here and they don't live here. And there it doesn't matter what passport you have, by the way. Stefan is actually Swiss, and he still has it. That surprised me as well the first time.
So someone living abroad and working here always does it?
Yes. And with them the calculator gets much more complicated, there are more questions. Germany has its own forms, I can never remember what they're called.
Okay, that's fine, the calculator will tell us. I think I have what I need. Is there anything you were hoping to cover that we didn't?
Only the timing. When can we have this?
I'll come back to you on that this week, once we've gone through your screenshots.
Good. I'll send them after lunch. Thanks, Leo.
Thanks, Anna. Talk soon.
